questions.title: What exactly is producer–consumer asynchrony in FlashAttention‑3 and how does warp‑specialization implement it?
questions.question_body: In Section 3 the authors say they split warps into producer and consumer groups and use a circular shared memory buffer to hide latency. I am unclear about three points: (a) what operations belong to a producer versus a consumer, (b) how the circular buffer coordinates loads of Q/K/V with computation, and (c) why this scheme improves occupancy on Hopper compared to the fully synchronous design used in FlashAttention‑2.

questions.title: How does ping‑pong scheduling overlap GEMM and softmax across warpgroups in FlashAttention‑3?
questions.question_body: The paper introduces a ping‑pong schedule where one warpgroup performs softmax while another runs WGMMA GEMMs. I would like a step‑by‑step illustration of which iteration’s softmax is paired with which iteration’s matrix multiplication, and why this pattern yields higher Tensor Core utilization than the original FlashAttention‑2 loop.

questions.title: What do SS‑GEMM and RS‑GEMM stand for in Algorithm 1?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 1 lines 9–15 the authors label two GEMM calls as SS‑GEMM and RS‑GEMM respectively. Are these abbreviations meant to indicate "shared–shared" versus "register–shared" operand locations, or something else? How does this affect register pressure and memory traffic?

questions.title: Why is softmax a performance bottleneck on H100 despite its low FLOP count?
questions.question_body: The authors state that exponential units deliver only ~3.9 TFLOP/s while Tensor Cores deliver ~989 TFLOP/s for FP16 matmul on H100. Could someone explain why softmax can occupy up to half of execution cycles even though it performs far fewer floating point operations than GEMM, and how overlapping it with async WGMMA resolves this imbalance?

questions.title: How is block quantization applied when converting Q, K, V tensors to FP8?
questions.question_body: Section 4 describes block quantization where each tile gets its own scaling factor before casting to FP8. I am unsure how these per‑tile scales are stored during execution, whether they are kept in registers or SMEM, and exactly where the scale multiplication takes place before feeding operands into WGMMA.

questions.title: What is incoherent processing with an orthogonal matrix M and why does it preserve attention results?
questions.question_body: The paper multiplies both Q and K by a random orthogonal matrix M prior to FP8 quantization (“incoherent processing”). I understand M · Mᵀ = I guarantees exact preservation of Q·Kᵀ mathematically, but I am confused whether applying M changes distribution of individual elements enough to improve quantization error without affecting downstream computations such as rotary embeddings.
